15: package caddyfile
16: 
17: import (
18: 	"bufio"
19: 	"bytes"
20: 	"fmt"
21: 	"io"
22: 	"regexp"
23: 	"strings"
24: 	"unicode"
25: )
26: 
27: type (
28: 	// lexer is a utility which can get values, token by
29: 	// token, from a Reader. A token is a word, and tokens
30: 	// are separated by whitespace. A word can be enclosed
31: 	// in quotes if it contains whitespace.
32: 	lexer struct {
33: 		reader       *bufio.Reader
34: 		token        Token
35: 		line         int
36: 		skippedLines int
37: 	}
38: 
39: 	// Token represents a single parsable unit.
40: 	Token struct {
41: 		File          string
42: 		origFile      string
43: 		Line          int
44: 		Text          string
45: 		wasQuoted     rune // enclosing quote character, if any
46: 		heredocMarker string
47: 		snippetName   string
48: 	}
49: )
50: 
51: // Tokenize takes bytes as input and lexes it into
52: // a list of tokens that can be parsed as a Caddyfile.
53: // Also takes a filename to fill the token's File as
54: // the source of the tokens, which is important to
55: // determine relative paths for `import` directives.
56: func Tokenize(input []byte, filename string) ([]Token, error) {
57: 	l := lexer{}
58: 	if err := l.load(bytes.NewReader(input)); err != nil {
59: 		return nil, err
60: 	}
61: 	var tokens []Token
62: 	for {
63: 		found, err := l.next()
64: 		if err != nil {
65: 			return nil, err
66: 		}
67: 		if !found {
68: 			break
69: 		}
70: 		l.token.File = filename
71: 		tokens = append(tokens, l.token)
72: 	}
73: 	return tokens, nil
74: }
75: 
76: // load prepares the lexer to scan an input for tokens.
77: // It discards any leading byte order mark.
78: func (l *lexer) load(input io.Reader) error {
79: 	l.reader = bufio.NewReader(input)
80: 	l.line = 1
81: 
82: 	// discard byte order mark, if present
83: 	firstCh, _, err := l.reader.ReadRune()
84: 	if err != nil {
85: 		return err
86: 	}
87: 	if firstCh != 0xFEFF {
88: 		err := l.reader.UnreadRune()
89: 		if err != nil {
90: 			return err
91: 		}
92: 	}
93: 
94: 	return nil
95: }
96: 
97: // next loads the next token into the lexer.
98: // A token is delimited by whitespace, unless
99: // the token starts with a quotes character (")
100: // in which case the token goes until the closing
101: // quotes (the enclosing quotes are not included).
102: // Inside quoted strings, quotes may be escaped
103: // with a preceding \ character. No other chars
104: // may be escaped. The rest of the line is skipped
105: // if a "#" character is read in. Returns true if
106: // a token was loaded; false otherwise.
107: func (l *lexer) next() (bool, error) {
108: 	var val []rune
109: 	var comment, quoted, btQuoted, inHeredoc, heredocEscaped, escaped bool
110: 	var heredocMarker string
111: 
112: 	makeToken := func(quoted rune) bool {
113: 		l.token.Text = string(val)
114: 		l.token.wasQuoted = quoted
115: 		l.token.heredocMarker = heredocMarker
116: 		return true
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	for {
120: 		// Read a character in; if err then if we had
121: 		// read some characters, make a token. If we
122: 		// reached EOF, then no more tokens to read.
123: 		// If no EOF, then we had a problem.
124: 		ch, _, err := l.reader.ReadRune()
125: 		if err != nil {
126: 			if len(val) > 0 {
127: 				if inHeredoc {
128: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("incomplete heredoc <<%s on line #%d, expected ending marker %s", heredocMarker, l.line+l.skippedLines, heredocMarker)
129: 				}
130: 
131: 				return makeToken(0), nil
132: 			}
133: 			if err == io.EOF {
134: 				return false, nil
135: 			}
136: 			return false, err
137: 		}
138: 
139: 		// detect whether we have the start of a heredoc
140: 		if !inHeredoc && !heredocEscaped && len(val) > 1 && string(val[:2]) == "<<" {
141: 			if ch == '<' {
142: 				return false, fmt.Errorf("too many '<' for heredoc on line #%d; only use two, for example <<END", l.line)
143: 			}
144: 			if ch == '\r' {
145: 				continue
146: 			}
147: 			// after hitting a newline, we know that the heredoc marker
148: 			// is the characters after the two << and the newline.
149: 			// we reset the val because the heredoc is syntax we don't
150: 			// want to keep.
151: 			if ch == '\n' {
152: 				heredocMarker = string(val[2:])
153: 				if !heredocMarkerRegexp.Match([]byte(heredocMarker)) {
154: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("heredoc marker on line #%d must contain only alpha-numeric characters, dashes and underscores; got '%s'", l.line, heredocMarker)
155: 				}
156: 
157: 				inHeredoc = true
158: 				l.skippedLines++
159: 				val = nil
160: 				continue
161: 			}
162: 			val = append(val, ch)
163: 			continue
164: 		}
165: 
166: 		// if we're in a heredoc, all characters are read as-is
167: 		if inHeredoc {
168: 			val = append(val, ch)
169: 
170: 			if ch == '\n' {
171: 				l.skippedLines++
172: 			}
173: 
174: 			// check if we're done, i.e. that the last few characters are the marker
175: 			if len(val) > len(heredocMarker) && heredocMarker == string(val[len(val)-len(heredocMarker):]) {
176: 				// set the final value
177: 				val, err = l.finalizeHeredoc(val, heredocMarker)
178: 				if err != nil {
179: 					return false, err
180: 				}
181: 
182: 				// set the line counter, and make the token
183: 				l.line += l.skippedLines
184: 				l.skippedLines = 0
185: 				return makeToken('<'), nil
186: 			}
187: 
188: 			// stay in the heredoc until we find the ending marker
189: 			continue
190: 		}
191: 
192: 		// track whether we found an escape '\' for the next
193: 		// iteration to be contextually aware
194: 		if !escaped && !btQuoted && ch == '\\' {
195: 			escaped = true
196: 			continue
197: 		}
198: 
199: 		if quoted || btQuoted {
200: 			if quoted && escaped {
201: 				// all is literal in quoted area,
202: 				// so only escape quotes
203: 				if ch != '"' {
204: 					val = append(val, '\\')
205: 				}
206: 				escaped = false
207: 			} else {
208: 				if (quoted && ch == '"') || (btQuoted && ch == '`') {
209: 					return makeToken(ch), nil
210: 				}
211: 			}
212: 			// allow quoted text to wrap continue on multiple lines
213: 			if ch == '\n' {
214: 				l.line += 1 + l.skippedLines
215: 				l.skippedLines = 0
216: 			}
217: 			// collect this character as part of the quoted token
218: 			val = append(val, ch)
219: 			continue
220: 		}
221: 
222: 		if unicode.IsSpace(ch) {
223: 			// ignore CR altogether, we only actually care about LF (\n)
224: 			if ch == '\r' {
225: 				continue
226: 			}
227: 			// end of the line
228: 			if ch == '\n' {
229: 				// newlines can be escaped to chain arguments
230: 				// onto multiple lines; else, increment the line count
231: 				if escaped {
232: 					l.skippedLines++
233: 					escaped = false
234: 				} else {
235: 					l.line += 1 + l.skippedLines
236: 					l.skippedLines = 0
237: 				}
238: 				// comments (#) are single-line only
239: 				comment = false
240: 			}
241: 			// any kind of space means we're at the end of this token
242: 			if len(val) > 0 {
243: 				return makeToken(0), nil
244: 			}
245: 			continue
246: 		}
247: 
248: 		// comments must be at the start of a token,
249: 		// in other words, preceded by space or newline
250: 		if ch == '#' && len(val) == 0 {
251: 			comment = true
252: 		}
253: 		if comment {
254: 			continue
255: 		}
256: 
257: 		if len(val) == 0 {
258: 			l.token = Token{Line: l.line}
259: 			if ch == '"' {
260: 				quoted = true
261: 				continue
262: 			}
263: 			if ch == '`' {
264: 				btQuoted = true
265: 				continue
266: 			}
267: 		}
268: 
269: 		if escaped {
270: 			// allow escaping the first < to skip the heredoc syntax
271: 			if ch == '<' {
272: 				heredocEscaped = true
273: 			} else {
274: 				val = append(val, '\\')
275: 			}
276: 			escaped = false
277: 		}
278: 
279: 		val = append(val, ch)
280: 	}
281: }
282: 
283: // finalizeHeredoc takes the runes read as the heredoc text and the marker,
284: // and processes the text to strip leading whitespace, returning the final
285: // value without the leading whitespace.
286: func (l *lexer) finalizeHeredoc(val []rune, marker string) ([]rune, error) {
287: 	// find the last newline of the heredoc, which is where the contents end
288: 	lastNewline := strings.LastIndex(string(val), "\n")
289: 
290: 	// collapse the content, then split into separate lines
291: 	lines := strings.Split(string(val[:lastNewline+1]), "\n")
292: 
293: 	// figure out how much whitespace we need to strip from the front of every line
294: 	// by getting the string that precedes the marker, on the last line
295: 	paddingToStrip := string(val[lastNewline+1 : len(val)-len(marker)])
296: 
297: 	// iterate over each line and strip the whitespace from the front
298: 	var out string
299: 	for lineNum, lineText := range lines[:len(lines)-1] {
300: 		// find an exact match for the padding
301: 		index := strings.Index(lineText, paddingToStrip)
302: 
303: 		// if the padding doesn't match exactly at the start then we can't safely strip
304: 		if index != 0 {
305: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("mismatched leading whitespace in heredoc <<%s on line #%d [%s], expected whitespace [%s] to match the closing marker", marker, l.line+lineNum+1, lineText, paddingToStrip)
306: 		}
307: 
308: 		// strip, then append the line, with the newline, to the output.
309: 		// also removes all "\r" because Windows.
310: 		out += strings.ReplaceAll(lineText[len(paddingToStrip):]+"\n", "\r", "")
311: 	}
312: 
313: 	// return the final value
314: 	return []rune(out), nil
315: }
316: 
317: // originalFile gets original filename before import modification.
318: func (t Token) originalFile() string {
319: 	if t.origFile != "" {
320: 		return t.origFile
321: 	}
322: 	return t.File
323: }
324: 
325: // updateFile updates the token's source filename for error display
326: // and remembers the original filename. Used during "import" processing.
327: func (t *Token) updateFile(file string) {
328: 	if t.origFile == "" {
329: 		t.origFile = t.File
330: 	}
331: 	t.File = file
332: }
333: 
334: func (t Token) Quoted() bool {
335: 	return t.wasQuoted > 0
336: }
337: 
338: // NumLineBreaks counts how many line breaks are in the token text.
339: func (t Token) NumLineBreaks() int {
340: 	lineBreaks := strings.Count(t.Text, "\n")
341: 	if t.wasQuoted == '<' {
342: 		// heredocs have an extra linebreak because the opening
343: 		// delimiter is on its own line and is not included in
344: 		// the token Text itself
345: 		lineBreaks++
346: 	}
347: 	return lineBreaks
348: }
349: 
350: var heredocMarkerRegexp = regexp.MustCompile("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$")
